10 Two equal masses travel towards each other on a frictionless track at speeds of 60 cm s–1 and
30 cm s–1. They stick together on impact.
60 cm s–1
30 cm s–1
What is the speed of the masses after impact?
A
15 cm s–1
B
20 cm s–1
C
30 cm s–1
D
45 cm s–1

hints: Notice the $60\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ arrow points right and the $30\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ arrow points left, so give them opposite signs in momentum.
Recall total momentum before a perfectly inelastic collision equals $(m+m)v$ after, with each mass equal to $m$.
Set $m(60)+m(-30)=2mv$ and solve for $v$ to get the combined speed in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Take motion to the right as positive. The left mass has velocity $+60\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ and the right mass has velocity $-30\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
Let each mass be $m$. Total momentum before impact is $p = m(60) + m(-30) = 30m$ in units of $\text{g cm s}^{-1}$ if $m$ is in grams.
After impact they stick, so combined mass is $m+m = 2m$ moving with unknown velocity $v$.
Conservation of linear momentum on the frictionless track gives $2mv = 30m$.
Cancel $m$ to get $2v = 30$, so $v = 15\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to the right. This is option A.

A.explanation: Conservation of momentum gives $v = 15\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ in the original direction of the $60\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ mass.

B.explanation: This does not satisfy $m(60)-m(30)=2mv$ for equal masses sticking together.

C.explanation: This ignores vector signs and treats the $30\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ as if it adds fully instead of partly cancelling.

D.explanation: This is the average of the speeds, $(60+30)/2$, which ignores opposite directions and doubling of mass.
